previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder, and a chronic indwelling Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness and fever. He was diagnosed with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia and a urinary tract infection, likely originating from his catheter and a bladder stone. His creatinine was elevated on admission due to dehydration, which resolved with IV fluids. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy, and he underwent surgical lithotripsy to remove the infected bladder stone. Blood cultures cleared, and his white count normalized. He was discharged to an extended care facility to complete a 6-day course of IV cefepime, with plans for weekly Foley catheter changes and initiation of methenamine and vitamin C for UTI suppression. Follow-up with infectious disease was arranged.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Urinary tract infection, site not specified

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with PMH of MS with neurogenic bladder requiring chronic 
indwelling foley and recurrent urosepsis who came in for sepsis 
with a UTI, bacteremia and infected Stage IV decub w/ evidence 
of osteo, treated with IV Abx.

*** Active Diagnoses ***
.
#Sepsis due to Osteomyelitis
Stage IV sacral decub on admission that appeared infected and 
required debridement by ACS that was probed to bone with 
elevated ESR/CRP suggestive of osteomyletitis. BLood cultures 
positive for skin flora - likely true infection from sacral 
wound.  Patient was started and continued on IV vanc/zosyn for 
broad coverage as no cultures/biopsies for narrowing abx was 
available. ID saw pt and recommended 6 week course of 
antibiotics with follow-up in 2 weeks. After initial date of 
admission, had been afebrile throughout hospital course with 
improved leukocytosis.  Discharged to ___ for careful wound 
care with potential need for further debridement. 
.
# Recurrent UTI
History of recurrent urosepsis due to indwelling foley for his 
neurogenic bladder from MS. ___ consistent with a UTI but UCx 
grew mutli-organism. ___ was replaced. On prior admits, 
culture data has shown pseudomonas (resistant to cipro), 
enterococcus (sensitive to vanco), ESBL E.coli (sensitive to 
zosyn). Pt started on IV vanc/zosyn with plans to continue for 6 
weeks for above osteo. Pt will need to follow-up with his 
urologist to discuss suprapubic catheter placement which he now 
is more receptive to (has refused previously). 
.
# Diplopia and Dizziness
Appears that his diplopia is consistent with his known R eye 
esotropia and pt reports these happen to him time to time. 
Resolved on its own within an hour before stat CTA head and neck 
could be obtained so decision was to not scan given unlikely 
stroke. Likely triggered by anesthesia given for debridement.  
Dizziness seems posisbly relatd to lack of PO intake that 
improved with IVF therapy. Since episode that occurred during 
admission, had not had the complaint further. 
.
# Moderate malnutrition: 
with weight loss and low albumin.  Seen by nutrition.  Likely 
triggered by lack of access to high protein/calorie snacks and 
foods at home as he is bedbound.  Had good PO intake in 
hospital.  Will need increased home services upon discharge from 
rehab. 
.

# Chronic Anemia

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Fever, evaluate for pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  Single portable frontal chest radiograph demonstrates well-expanded
lungs.  Heart is normal in size, and cardiomediastinal contours are
unremarkable.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  Small calcified
granulomas are again noted.  The lungs are otherwise clear.  Lower cervical
fusion hardware noted.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of pneumonia.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___, Dr. ___ and Dr. ___, the
attending radiologist, performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the patent right
basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a
micropuncture set. Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and
immediately after establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was
then placed over a guidewire and a dual-lumen PICC line measuring 40-cm in
length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in
the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed
by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

Total radiation dose: 3 mGy

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically-guided double-lumen
PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final internal
length is 40 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready to use.
